actions.definition: Two unit actions through the same forward function, the roster as signed: hire one AE starting 2026-09-01; add $1,000,000 of program pipeline starting 2026-09-01. Gain per dollar is the bookings gained in the next twelve months over the cash cost inside the same twelve months. An action starts paying in the first month it adds at least 1% of its twelve-month gain.
actions.meaning: 'feasible' means achievable inside the model's bounds, not operationally achievable; that a new hire adds pipeline at the fitted rate is an assumption
actions.program_shape: created from 2026-09 to the fiscal-year end, ramping up over the entered ramp (3 months unless capacity.yaml says otherwise)

ranges.method: Each side's factor is the ceil(90% of n)-th smallest of the factors the n eligible past forecasts would have needed: the plain empirical rule, not a finite-sample guarantee. Six-month factors come from overlapping forecasts (each shares five of its six months with its neighbors) and are noisier: 11 past six-month forecasts to learn from, 1 scored.
ranges.reason: pooled over 1 and 3 months, 18 scored folds: simulated 16 held (89%), stretched 16 held (89%); the stretched coverage is not closer to 80%
ranges.rule: adopted if there are at least 6 scored folds at 1 and at 3 months, pooled 80% coverage over 1 and 3 months is closer to 80% than the simulated range's on the same folds, and no horizon (1, 3 or 6 months) moves more than 10 points further from 80%; each side's factor is the smallest, never below 1, that would have put at least 90% of the eligible past folds inside on that side (a fold is eligible once its whole horizon has ended; at least 5 are needed)

recency.reason: lower mean absolute error at 1 and 3 months (1m: 998,999 vs 1,384,619; 3m: 1,944,676 vs 2,261,995)
recency.rule: adopted only if the fitted model's mean absolute error is lower than the Goal 1 fit's at both 1 and 3 months, on the same folds (at least 6 at each)

backtest.reason: the model's mean absolute error is not lower than every baseline: 3m: model 1,944,676 vs trailing run-rate 1,942,333; 3m: model 1,944,676 vs stage-weighted pipeline 1,776,756
backtest.scoring: per horizon, mean absolute dollar error over all folds; 'yes' only if the fitted model's error is lower than both baselines at 1 and 3 months; under 6 folds is 'not enough history to say'

driver_actions.definition: A driver action is a named change to one driver in one slice, with a start month, a ramp and a target. It changes the pipeline created from its start, ramping linearly by creation date to the target and holding it after. Pipeline created before the start, and every deal already open, keeps the rates, sizes and counts it had. Where the capacity term is in use, hires and programs stay as the plan has them; each action is valued against them. A target is read against the pooled baseline of its driver; for a segment it is an entered change on that baseline, not a value that was measured for the segment. Actions on different drivers add their changes to the plan as it stands without them, and work through each win together.

items.affects: Pipeline created from October 2026 in Enterprise, ramping up over 2 months to the target; pipeline created earlier, and every deal already open, keeps its rate.
items.name: Enterprise win-rate push

items.affects: Wins of pipeline created from October 2026 in Company, ramping up over 1 month to the target size; how many are won, and the wins of pipeline created earlier or already open, keep their size.

items.affects: The deals Mid Market creates itself from November 2026, through its people, ramping up over 2 months to the target; the deals programs create, deals created earlier and every deal already open stay as they were.

driver_actions.line: An action changes one driver of the pipeline created from its start month on: the win rate, the size of a win, how many deals people create, or how long wins take. Deals already open keep their odds, their size and their timing. A segment's target is an entered change on the pooled baseline, not a value measured for the segment.
driver_actions.range_note: The plan's ranges are simulated with the actions in force, so they carry the model's uncertainty under the actions and exclude uncertainty about whether an action is achieved.

sentences.next twelve months: What removing each one changes adds up to more than the actions change together: each does more with the others in place, because their changes multiply, so they reinforce each other.
sentences.rest of fiscal year: What removing each one changes adds up to more than the actions change together: each does more with the others in place, because their changes multiply, so they reinforce each other.

driver_actions.removal_note: Each action's value is the forecast with all the actions less the forecast with every other action but not this one, hires and programs held. It is what removing it loses, not a share of the joint gain, so the values need not add up to it.
driver_actions.rounding_note: Each forecast is the sum of its months, each to the cent. A figure that is a difference of forecasts can differ from another route to the same figure by up to a cent a month; the reconciliation line is held to that.

fiscal_year.why_they_differ: Meeting every quarter's own target is stricter than meeting the year's total: a quarter that is ahead cannot lend its surplus to one that is behind, and pipeline created in a quarter mostly books after it.

lead_time.basis: the production forward function's own timing, on a probe dollar-amount created evenly through the month; independent of the capacity decision. These are dollar yields, not probabilities: amounts change between creation and win, so they can exceed or fall short of what the deal counts imply and are not forced to sum to one

count_outcome.meaning: of the deals created, from the fit in use; counts, so these sum to one

lead_time.question: of a dollar of pipeline created next month (at its first recorded amount), the cents booked by the end of each of the next four quarters

required_pipeline.meaning: 'required' means achievable inside the model's bounds (fitted conversion and timing, the cap above), not operationally achievable
required_pipeline.method: one deterministic solve in quarter order; each quarter's pipeline is created evenly on every day from the day after the as-of date to its end (creation starts now), and meets that quarter's target given its actual bookings, the pipeline already open and what earlier quarters were assigned; an unreachable quarter is assigned nothing. Pipeline assigned to a later quarter is also created in the earlier quarters' months, so it can only add to them

per_rep_rule.why: capacity is the forecast's basis, so the team's best per ramped AE-month is a third leg beside the cap and the total rate

required_pipeline.too_late_rule: a quarter is too late to fund with new pipeline when its requirement is over the cap (or the cap is used up, or no pipeline created in time can book inside it), or when everything created in its span (expected, earlier quarters' assignments and its own requirement) per day is above the team's best four-quarter average of total created pipeline per day, or, only where capacity is the forecast's basis, when that total per ramped AE-month is above the team's best; the reason names exactly the legs that fired

worksheet.definition: What moves the outcome: four operating drivers, each changed alone for deals created after the as-of date, measured around the plan in force.

drivers.applies_to: The share of deals created after the as-of date that are won, for organic, hire-generated and program pipeline alike. Open deals and actuals are untouched.

historical.rule: The low and high settings are the means of the lower and the upper half of the observed quarters; with an odd number of quarters the middle one is in neither half.

drivers.label: Win rate of new pipeline
drivers.limitation: The fit in use learns from every deal created in its recent window, young deals included, while these quarters are complete and matured, so they are older than that fit and may not describe it. The plan's win-rate actions add their points to the pooled rate this changes, each day's rate held between zero and one, so bookings are not a straight line in it: no setting is solved for, and the changes at the low and high settings are not on one line.

drivers.applies_to: The mean ARR of each win among deals created after the as-of date. Creation counts and the program dollars-to-deals conversion are unchanged.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when its deals have had the full horizon to win and at least five of them were won.

drivers.label: Won ARR per new win
drivers.limitation: The fit in use learns from every deal created in its recent window, young deals included, while these quarters are complete and matured, so they are older than that fit and may not describe it. The plan's size actions change the size this sets by the same relative amount, so a setting here is the pooled mean the actions are measured from, and the changes shown are the plan with its actions in force at that setting.

needed_alone.history_label: Inside what the company has done: the value lies between the lowest and the highest quarter observed.
needed_alone.outcome_label: Solves mathematically: this value, alone, takes fiscal-year bookings to target.

drivers.unit_label: dollars of ARR per won deal

drivers.applies_to: Deals created per ramped AE-month, for the signed roster and any planned hires, after the as-of date. Open deals and actuals are untouched.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when at least twenty deals were created in it and there was capacity to divide by. Creation is final the day a quarter ends, so there is no waiting.

historical.rule: The low and high settings are the means of the lower and the upper half of the observed quarters; with an odd number of quarters the middle one is in neither half.

drivers.label: Creation productivity
drivers.limitation: Each quarter is read against the current fitted ramp curve and the roster that actually worked, not against a curve refitted for that quarter. The plan's creation actions change the rate this sets by the same relative amount, so a setting here is the pooled rate the actions are measured from, and the changes shown are the plan with its actions in force at that setting.

evidence.gate: A quarter counts when its deals have had the full horizon to win and at least five of them were won.

historical.rule: The low and high settings are the means of the lower and the upper half of the observed quarters; with an odd number of quarters the middle one is in neither half.

drivers.label: Cycle length of new pipeline
drivers.limitation: The fit in use learns from every deal created in its recent window, young deals included, while these quarters are complete and matured, so they are older than that fit and may not describe it. A quarter's cycle is the plain mean days of its wins, while the fit in use weights each day, so the two are close in kind but not the same measure.

needed_alone.history_label: Inside what the company has done: the value lies between the lowest and the highest quarter observed.
needed_alone.outcome_label: Solves mathematically, stepped: win times are whole days, so there is no exact root. This is the largest setting that reaches the target, and it overshoots by the amount shown.

worksheet.expectation_note: Every figure here is an expected value from the forward function. No simulation is run, so no range is attached to any sensitivity.
worksheet.history_note: Historical settings describe what the company has done. They are not forecasts, they are not called achievable, and nothing here says they will happen again.
worksheet.measured_around: the plan in force: its hires, program pipeline and driver actions, as applied
worksheet.sensitivity_note: Each change is a conditional change in expected bookings, measured one driver at a time around the plan in force. It is not a forecast and not a cause, and the bars are never summed: drivers act together, not alone.
